paragraphs.text: We report efficient perovskite solar cells based on MAPbI3 absorbers. The champion device reached a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 21.1% under 1-sun illumination.
The reference device without interface engineering reached a PCE of 17.9%. Under identical 1-sun conditions, the engineered champion device outperforms the reference device.
J. Zhang fabricated the devices and wrote the manuscript. L. Chen measured the J-V curves. R. Okafor supervised the project.

Perovskite solar cells based on MAPbI3 have attracted intense interest because of their tunable bandgap and low-temperature processing. Interface engineering between the absorber and the charge-transport layers remains a key lever for efficiency.
MAPbI3 films were deposited by one-step spin-coating from a DMF precursor solution onto the prepared substrates. The films were annealed at 100 C for 10 min in a nitrogen glovebox.
The device architecture was glass/ITO/compact TiO2/mesoporous TiO2/MAPbI3/spiro-OMeTAD/Au. All devices in this study share this architecture and are referred to as device A.
The mesoporous TiO2 layer of device A was sintered at 500 C before absorber deposition. This layer serves as the electron-transport layer of the champion device.
Current density-voltage curves were recorded under AM1.5G 1-sun illumination at a scan rate of 100 mV/s using a calibrated solar simulator.
The champion device reached a PCE of 21.1% in the initial 1-sun measurement, with an open-circuit voltage of 1.11 V. This is the best initial value we have obtained for this architecture.
After 100 h of shelf storage in the dark, the unencapsulated champion device retained a PCE of 19.8%. Shelf storage is a milder stress than damp-heat aging.
We attribute the high initial efficiency to the dense, pinhole-free MAPbI3 morphology observed by SEM. The engineered interface appears to suppress interfacial recombination.
We study the damp-heat stability of methylammonium lead iodide solar cells. After 500 h at 85 C and 85% relative humidity, encapsulated devices retained 18.7% PCE.
S. Patel designed the aging experiments. L. Chen contributed to the aging experiments and device characterization.

Methylammonium lead iodide (MAPbI3) is the most widely studied perovskite absorber. Its long-term stability under heat and humidity remains the main barrier to commercialization.
Zhang et al. previously reported a PCE of 21.1% for MAPbI3 devices under 1-sun illumination. That value represents an initial efficiency, not a post-aging result.
Our devices used a compact TiO2 electron-transport layer deposited by spray pyrolysis, a sample distinct from mesoporous architectures. We refer to this device stack as device B.
Devices were encapsulated with a glass-glass edge seal before aging. Encapsulation was verified by visual inspection and weight gain tests.
Damp-heat aging followed IEC 61215: 85 C and 85% relative humidity for 500 h. Devices were removed periodically for characterization under 1-sun illumination.
After 500 h of damp-heat aging, the best device retained a PCE of 18.7%, measured under 1-sun illumination. The unaged control device of the same batch measured 20.2% PCE.
The hysteresis index was not measured in this study. We caution that scan-rate effects were therefore not quantified.
The retained efficiency after aging is not directly comparable to the initial 21.1% reported by Zhang et al., because the measurement conditions differ. Both values are nonetheless informative.
